faq.question: How much does window replacement cost in Cloverdale?
faq.answer: Cloverdale homeowners typically invest $4,500 to $10,000 for a full window replacement project. This Sonoma County wine country community has a modest housing stock, and most projects involve standard-sized windows in 1970s–1990s ranch homes. Single window installation starts at approximately $420.

faq.question: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Cloverdale?
faq.answer: Yes. Cloverdale requires a building permit for window replacements. Our team manages all permit applications and scheduling with the City of Cloverdale Building Department on your behalf.

faq.question: Is it worth replacing 20-year-old windows in Cloverdale?
faq.answer: Often yes. Twenty-year-old windows in Cloverdale commonly show fogged glass, drafts and weak locks. Newer ENERGY STAR units improve comfort and curb appeal; Deluxe Windows compares payback against your utility rates and home style before recommending replacement.

faq.question: Should I choose fiberglass or vinyl windows in Cloverdale?
faq.answer: Vinyl is the value pick for most Cloverdale replacements and handles Bay Area weather well. Fiberglass (including Marvin Ultrex) is stronger, more stable in temperature swings and better for larger openings or coastal exposure. We show both side by side in the showroom and on-site.

faq.question: How long does window replacement take in Cloverdale?
faq.answer: Most Cloverdale projects are measured in one visit and installed in one to three working days once products arrive — typically four to eight weeks after ordering, depending on brand and custom sizes.
